summary: A non-empty transcript from one sync path is not evidence that it is complete: Granola applies transcript retention upstream while this local store is expected to outlive it, so a sync must never delete a stored transcript to replace it with a SMALLER one owned by the other path. Ownership transfer stays as-is when the incoming copy is at least as complete (a whole-meeting rewrite is required either way, or the two sources collide on the transcript_segments (meeting_id, idx) primary key); the shrinking cross-source case keeps what is stored, skips the incoming write for that meeting, and reports a count plus the meeting ids on the same non-fatal warning channel as the unparsed-timestamp accounting. Size is compared only against the OTHER row_source, so a path rewriting its own earlier transcript is never blocked.
reason: The prior rule treated any non-empty payload as authoritative and ran an unscoped per-meeting DELETE, so the first API sync after upstream retention pruned an older meeting destroyed the full cache-captured transcript and left the remnant, permanently and with no count anywhere in the sync summary. Silence was half the defect: without the preserved-transcript accounting a user cannot distinguish a sync that correctly declined to shrink a transcript from one that is quietly broken.
validated_outcome: Against the pre-fix code the new store-level tests fail with 'the retention-pruned API transcript destroyed the larger cache-sourced one: got 2, want 5' and the mirror 'got 1, want 6'. An existing collision test had to move from a shorter to a longer incoming transcript, since the shorter direction is now the preservation case.
